nodes.name: Read Health
nodes.notes: neverError plus fullResponse so an unreachable orchestrator becomes a reportable state rather than a silent workflow failure. The URL is the compose-internal orchestrator hostname and is literal because N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=true blocks $env.

nodes.name: Diff Readiness
nodes.notes: Returning an empty array when nothing changed is what makes this quiet by default. Silence means no change. Every watched key is verified against the /health response builder in main.py: paid_runs_enabled is top level, the langgraph_primary keys come from primary_default.health() or the disabled-path literals, and kill_switch_open lives under parallel_dispatch (from parallel_dispatch_health_readiness), not langgraph_primary. Its polarity is inverted: open means the switch is NOT engaged, so the alarm fires on false. The seven provider_*_ready fields are boolean-only projections of health.providers; they report credential readiness, not native activation evidence. Provider changes produce one notice; unchanged readiness remains quiet unless another alarm applies.

nodes.name: Post Status
nodes.notes: docker-compose.yml sets N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=true, so $env in an expression resolves to an access-denied error, not a value. The channel is therefore a UI-bound placeholder: set it once in the n8n editor. No channel ID is committed to the repository.
